title: Two 3d–4f nanomagnets formed via a two-step in situ reaction of picolinaldehyde

synthesis.procedure: The article describes formation through a two-step in situ reaction of picolinaldehyde in the presence of Dy(III) and Cu(II). It states that increasing the concentration of all reactants yields complex 1, which incorporates both the gem-diol intermediate L² and hemiacetal product L³; it does not give a quantified preparation.

reagents.name: picolinaldehyde
reagents.role: precursor to in situ ligands L² and L³

synthesis.time: Stirred for 10 min; crystals obtained several days later.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: The blue solution was filtered, and the filtrate was left to evaporate, yielding blue crystals.

properties.summary: Complex 1 shows predominantly ferromagnetic interactions and slow magnetic relaxation characteristic of single-molecule-magnet behavior under zero external field.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Two DyCu₂ triangular units share a Dy corner and are crossed at Dy–Cu edges by L³ ligands. The resulting two butterfly-like DyCu₄ units join at their wing apexes to form the Dy₂Cu₇ double-butterfly cluster. Unlike complex 2, it incorporates both gem-diol-derived L² and hemiacetal L³.

synthesis.procedure: The article describes formation through a two-step in situ reaction of picolinaldehyde in the presence of Gd(III) and Cu(II), producing hemiacetal ligand L³ bound in complex 2. It does not give a quantified preparation.

reagents.name: picolinaldehyde
reagents.role: precursor to in situ hemiacetal ligand L³

synthesis.time: Stirred for 10 min; crystals obtained several days later.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: The blue solution was filtered, and the filtrate was left to evaporate, yielding blue crystals.

properties.summary: Complex 2 shows predominantly antiferromagnetic interactions and a significant magnetocaloric effect, supporting its characterization as a molecular magnetic refrigerant.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Six vertex-sharing Gd₂Cu₂ tetrahedral units, linked by hemiacetal ligands L³, form a hexagonal Gd₆Cu₁₂ wheel. The article proposes that a central nitrate anion may template construction of the hexagon.
